patch.value: The budget-exhaustion path and the sorted-run traversal were both asserted vacuously

CodeRabbit review of pm-rl#12, one Major and one Trivial, sharing a root: an assertion that holds whether or not the behaviour it names is present.

BUDGET EXHAUSTION was never proven. The test used a zero-permission approval, and the refusal fires at a count of zero whatever countPromotedUnderApproval returns, so the counting walk was never exercised. Its second case promoted the same generation twice and expected already promoted - a guard that runs BEFORE the budget check is reached, so that attempt never touched the budget path either. No case promoted DISTINCT candidates up to the limit.

This compounds the mutation-testing lesson from this same review. I had reported the budget refusal proven revert-proof by mutation at 31 of 32 passing. It fired because the zero-permission case trips it regardless. The count that actually bounds a recursive loop was untested.

SORTED RUN TRAVERSAL was likewise undiscriminating: only one run in the fixture mapped to the evaluation environment, so the match was found under insertion order too, and removing the sort would fail nothing.

Both assertions now discriminate, each verified by mutation.

Budget exhaustion: the test promotes distinct candidates gen-c2 and gen-c3 against a two-permission approval, then registers gen-c4 and asserts the third promotion is refused, that the message reports 2 promotion(s) consumed rather than merely firing, and that it names the approval item to extend. Proof it exercises the counter: suppressing the increment inside countPromotedUnderApproval turns the suite red at 23 of 24. Before this case, that mutation passed.

Sorted traversal: both runs in the fixture now reach the evaluation environment, so only the sort decides which is reported, and the assertion names the lexicographically first id. Proof: removing the sort() turns the suite red at 23 of 24.

release:check green, coverage still an exact 100/100/100 across 9 files.
